insight.title: How the Entire World Stays Connected Through Glass
insight.subtitle: Beneath the ocean waves, a vast network of cables carries our digital lives.

sections.text: Most people think the internet lives in the sky or inside satellites. In reality, nearly all global data travels through thin glass wires hidden deep under the sea. These fiber optic cables are about the size of a garden hose. They stretch for thousands of miles to link every continent together.

Inside these cables, your photos and messages turn into pulses of laser light. This light bounces off the walls of the glass core at incredible speeds. It moves so fast that a signal can travel across the Atlantic Ocean in less than a second. This makes instant communication possible everywhere.

To protect the fragile glass, engineers wrap it in layers of steel, plastic, and copper. These heavy lines rest on the dark ocean floor, avoiding underwater mountains and currents. Ships work constantly to maintain this invisible web. Without these undersea threads, our modern, hyper-connected world would simply go silent.

news.title: Study Reveals What Tau PET Scans Are Actually Seeing
news.description: Researchers use AI and postmortem tissue to reveal that tau PET scans are often influenced by iron and neuroinflammation rather than tau tangles alone.

news.title: PM Narendra Modi Launches Nationwide HPV Vaccination Drive for 14-Year-Old Girls
news.description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi launched a nationwide HPV vaccination campaign for 14-year-old girls from Ajmer, Rajasthan. The single-dose Gardasil 4 vaccine will be administered at government health facilities across India to prevent cervical cancer.

news.title: Why Your Brain Gets Sharper After Adolescence
news.description: Researchers identify that the brain's sensory checkpoint (TRN) undergoes a molecular "upgrade" in adulthood for high-resolution perception.
